newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Meridor wants civil service hiring cut.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Meridor wants civil service hiring cut.

text.p: Israeli Finance Minister Dan Meridor said he envisages limiting the hiring of new civil servants as a way of achieving further budget cuts next year.
"We want to prevent the entry, as much as possible, of new workers to the public sector," he said in an interview with Israel's Channel One television.
But he appeared to suggest that layoffs would not be necessary.

"Every year there is a natural attrition of about four percent -- people reach retirement age, people leave," Meridor said. "If you prevent entry (of new workers), you are already achieving a serious cut."
Meridor said the Treasury had still not determined where it would make the approximately two billion shekels in new spending cuts to be submitted to parliament next month.
He repeated that the government did not seek to increase the tax burden on Israelis. "The preferred way is not to raise taxes but to lower expenditures," Meridor said.
He warned that if parliament did not approve the Treasury's 1997 budget, unemployment and inflation would rise.

Meridor faces strong opposition in parliament to the budget, which originally called for 4.9 billion shekels in cuts. Earlier this week, Meridor said he would seek an additional two billion shekels in reductions.
